glosses: To find or learn something for the first time.

examples.text: Turning the corner, I discovered a lovely little shop. I discovered that they sold widgets.
All this has led to an explosion of protest across China, including among a middle class that has discovered nimbyism.

glosses: To remove the cover from; to uncover (a head, building etc.).

examples.text: He set down his bags beside him, on the beautiful red floor, and he took off his hat, for he had reached his destination, discovering his scant red hair, and laid it on the table beside him.

glosses: To expose, uncover.

examples.text: The gust of wind discovered a bone in the sand.

glosses: To create by moving a piece out of another piece's line of attack.

examples.text: This move discovers an attack on a vital pawn.

glosses: To question (a person) as part of discovery in a lawsuit.

examples.text: Indeed, the plaintiffs suggest that they may not need to call Ms. Samji at all if they are allowed to discover the defendant on the new documents before any new trial takes place.

glosses: To reveal (information); to divulge, make known.

examples.text: I discovered my plans to the rest of the team.
Go, draw aside the curtains, and discover / The several caskets to this noble prince.
Prosperity doth best discover vice; but adversity doth best discover virtue.
It was in vain to diſcover my Reſentments, which were always turned into Ridicule; and I was forced to reſt with Patience while my noble and moſt beloved Country was ſo injuriouſly treated.

glosses: To reconnoitre, explore (an area).

glosses: To manifest without design; to show; to exhibit.

examples.text: The youth discovered a taste for sculpture.
The English Cooks keep all their Spices in separate boxes, but the French Cooks make a spicey mixture that does not discover a predominancy of any one of the spices over the others.

glosses: To discover, as by asking or investigating.

examples.text: I don't know who the twenty-first president of the United States was, but it should be very easy to find out.

glosses: To discover or expose (someone) as disobedient, dishonest, etc.

examples.text: He had been fiddling the books for years, but finally he was found out.

glosses: To uncover a weakness in (someone).

examples.text: He may cope with the multiple choice questions, but the written exam will find him out.
If you don't try, you do not find it out.

glosses: To discover (something), as by perceiving or coming upon it.
To receive the consequences of one's actions.

examples.text: With the way he behaved, it's no wonder he found out.

glosses: Avanzar y llegar hasta algo o alguien que va adelante, física o figuradamente.

examples.text: Salí después que ellos, pero los alcancé porque corrí más rápido.

glosses: Llegar a tener algo que se deseaba o buscaba.

examples.text: Juan alcanzó un lugar en el evento.

glosses: Coger alguna cosa alargando la mano para tomarla.

examples.text: Con una mano alcanzo (a tomar) el vaso de cristal.

glosses: Avanzar hasta tocar, juntarse o hacer impacto con algo o alguien.

examples.text: La bala perdida alcanzó a un peatón.

examples.text: Y sobre aquel hambriento colchón, un alfamar del mismo jaez, del cual el color yo no pude alcanzar.

glosses: Tener capacidad o poder para algo.

examples.text: El viento no fue tan fuerte, pero sí alcanzó a hacer daños.

glosses: Llegar a cierto punto, distancia o nivel.

examples.text: Desde aquí alcanzo a ver la montaña.

glosses: Ser o haber suficiente para un propósito.

examples.text: El dinero no le alcanza para tantos lujos que quiere darse.
